source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-271065:Diagonal player movement is not normalized when holding two movement keys
source_meta._title: Player movement at low speeds is biased towards cardinal directions

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2 in a single-player, default Superflat world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled so command blocks can be created and edited. Use only one player because the report's repeating command targets every player with @a. The deterministic layout below places an impulse command block at X=0, Y=4, Z=0, a repeating command block at X=1, Y=4, Z=0, and the starting point south of them at X=0.5, Y=4, Z=10.5. Both command blocks remain Unconditional and Needs Redstone. The lever-on-impulse arrangement and command-block input behavior were operationally checked against Minecraft Wiki documentation. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AQuasi-connectivity?utm_source=openai))
preconditions: Launch the affected Java Edition version 1.15.2, which is the first version listed by the report. Do not use fix version 25w02a.
Create a new single-player world using the default Superflat preset, Creative mode, and Allow Cheats: ON.
Use a world with only one player connected so the @a selector produces one armor-stand trail rather than trails for multiple players.
Ensure the Move Forward and Sneak actions are available. With default controls these are W and Left Shift.
Do not move the mouse during either measured walk. Camera yaw is set by the teleport command, and manual camera movement would invalidate the comparison.
Keep the lever OFF until the first measured run begins.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start an installation using Java Edition 1.15.2 and wait for the main menu.
steps.exact_input: Select or create a launcher installation for release 1.15.2, then click Play.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left corner of the Minecraft main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft 1.15.2.

steps.action: Create the test world as a Creative, cheat-enabled Superflat world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> cycle World Type to Superflat -> Done -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player loads into a flat grass world in Creative mode and can execute commands.

steps.action: Wait for the world to become ready before constructing the apparatus.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain has rendered, the player is standing on the flat surface, and movement and chat commands respond normally.

steps.action: Move the player to the deterministic construction area near the world origin.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/tp @s 0.5 4 4.5 180 0`, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the grass surface near X=0, Z=4.5 and is facing approximately north toward decreasing Z.

steps.action: Place the impulse command block at the defined test origin using a chat command.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/setblock 0 4 0 minecraft:command_block`, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: An orange impulse command block is visible on the surface at X=0, Y=4, Z=0.

steps.action: Place the repeating command block directly east of and adjacent to the impulse command block.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/setblock 1 4 0 minecraft:repeating_command_block`, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A purple repeating command block is visible at X=1, Y=4, Z=0, sharing a side with the impulse command block.

steps.action: Configure the impulse command block to teleport the nearest player to a point 10 blocks south of it with yaw 174 and pitch 0. Yaw 174 is six degrees away from north-facing yaw 180, as required by the report's south-of-the-blocks example.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the impulse command block at 0 4 0. In its command field enter `/tp @p 0.5 4 10.5 174 0`. Verify the buttons read Impulse, Unconditional, and Needs Redstone, then click Done.
steps.success_cue: The impulse command block has saved the teleport command and remains configured as Impulse, Unconditional, Needs Redstone.

steps.action: Configure the repeating command block with the report's exact armor-stand trail command.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the repeating command block at 1 4 0. Enter `/execute as @a as @s run summon minecraft:armor_stand ~ ~ ~ {Small:1b}` exactly, including `{Small:1b}`. Verify the buttons read Repeat, Unconditional, and Needs Redstone, then click Done.
steps.success_cue: The repeating command block has saved the exact report command and remains configured as Repeat, Unconditional, Needs Redstone.

steps.action: Obtain one lever for controlling both adjacent command blocks.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/give @s minecraft:lever 1`, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A lever is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Place the lever on the top face of the impulse command block without opening the command-block interface. Sneaking while placing allows the lever to be placed on an interactive block.
steps.exact_input: Select the lever in the hotbar. Hold Left Shift, right-click the top face of the impulse command block at 0 4 0, then release Left Shift.
steps.success_cue: An OFF lever is attached to the top of the impulse command block at approximately X=0, Y=5, Z=0. No teleport has occurred and no armor stands are spawning.

steps.action: Confirm the final command-block power configuration before beginning the measured runs.
steps.exact_input: Inspect each command block by right-clicking its exposed side if necessary. Confirm the impulse block is Impulse/Unconditional/Needs Redstone and the repeating block is Repeat/Unconditional/Needs Redstone. Close each interface with Done without changing the commands.
steps.success_cue: Both commands remain saved, both command blocks require redstone power, and the lever is still OFF.

steps.action: Position the player immediately south of the apparatus so the lever can be targeted before the teleport fires.
steps.exact_input: Press T, enter `/tp @s 0.5 4 2.5 180 0`, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The player stands about two blocks south of the impulse command block, on the ground and within interaction reach of the lever.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair directly at the lever, stop all movement, and then stop providing mouse movement.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until the lever is outlined under the crosshair. Release all movement keys, then physically stop moving the mouse or otherwise provide zero camera input.
steps.success_cue: The lever is under the crosshair, the player is stationary, and the lever remains OFF.

steps.action: Activate the lever to power both command blocks and initiate the normal-speed control run. Do not move the mouse after clicking.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once.
steps.success_cue: The lever's rising signal causes the player to arrive at X=0.5, Y=4, Z=10.5 with yaw 174 and pitch 0; the player is standing on the flat ground and the repeating command block is powered.

steps.action: Perform the normal-speed control walk without sneaking and without changing the camera angle.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold W. Do not press Left Shift and do not move the mouse.
steps.success_cue: The player moves forward from the teleported starting position toward the command-block apparatus at normal walking speed while small armor stands are left along the traversed route.

steps.action: Continue the normal-speed walk only until the player is close enough to reach the lever, then stop before adjusting the view.
steps.exact_input: Continue holding W until the command blocks are approximately 2 to 4 blocks ahead, then release W.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary near the apparatus and within right-click reach of the lever; the first armor-stand trail remains in the world.

steps.action: After forward movement has completely stopped, aim at the elevated lever and switch it OFF to stop the repeating command block.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse to place the crosshair on the lever, then right-click once.
steps.success_cue: The lever is visibly OFF, the player is not teleported by the falling signal, and new armor stands stop appearing.

steps.action: Prepare the second run from the same nearby position. Aim at the lever again, ensure neither W nor Left Shift is held, and stop moving the mouse.
steps.exact_input: Place the crosshair on the lever, release all movement and sneak inputs, then provide no further mouse movement.
steps.success_cue: The stationary player is within reach of the OFF lever and has the lever under the crosshair.

steps.action: Activate the lever a second time to reset the player to the identical starting coordinates and camera rotation for the slow, sneaking run.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once.
steps.success_cue: The player is again teleported to X=0.5, Y=4, Z=10.5 with yaw 174 and pitch 0, and the repeating command block is powered again.

steps.action: Begin the low-speed test movement by sneaking and moving forward while keeping the camera completely unchanged.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold Left Shift, then press and hold W while continuing to hold Left Shift. Do not move the mouse.
steps.success_cue: The player is visibly in the lowered sneaking posture and is moving forward from the same starting location toward the command blocks.

steps.action: Continue holding both movement inputs until the player is again close enough to operate the lever.
steps.exact_input: Keep holding W and Left Shift, with no mouse movement, until the command blocks are approximately 2 to 4 blocks ahead.
steps.success_cue: The player has traversed the test route while continuously sneaking and is within interaction reach of the lever; both runs' armor stands remain present.

steps.action: Stop the sneaking movement before changing the camera direction.
steps.exact_input: Release W, then release Left Shift. Keep the mouse stationary until both inputs are released.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary near the apparatus and is no longer moving or sneaking.

steps.action: Aim at the elevated lever after the measured movement has ended.
steps.exact_input: Move the mouse until the crosshair outlines the lever on top of the impulse command block.
steps.success_cue: The powered lever is under the crosshair and the player remains stationary.

steps.action: Switch the lever OFF once to stop further armor-stand summoning, then make no further movement through the recorded paths.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once.
steps.success_cue: The lever is OFF, the repeating command block is no longer summoning armor stands, the player remains near the apparatus, and the two completed armor-stand trails are available for the observation subsystem.

stor.handoff_condition: The normal-speed control run and the sneaking run have both been completed from the same teleport position and yaw. W and Left Shift are released, the player is stationary near the command blocks, the lever has just been switched OFF, the repeating command block has stopped summoning armor stands, and both recorded trails remain in place. Hand control to the observation subsystem to inspect the trails without moving through or removing them.
uncertainties: The report does not specify fixed world coordinates, so the command blocks at 0 4 0 and 1 4 0 and the starting point at 0.5 4 10.5 are deterministic practical choices that preserve the stated geometry: a flat plane, adjacent command blocks, and a starting point about 10 blocks directly south of them.

The report does not supply the complete teleport command or target selector. `/tp @p 0.5 4 10.5 174 0` is constructed from the report's requirement for a position south of the command blocks and yaw 174, six degrees away from north-facing yaw 180.

The report does not explicitly specify a game mode. Creative mode with cheats is selected because Java Edition command blocks must be created and edited with the necessary permissions; this is an execution requirement rather than a claimed bug condition.

The instruction to stop approximately 2 to 4 blocks from the apparatus operationalizes the report's phrase 'until you are close to the lever.' The exact endpoint is not asserted to affect reproduction as long as the same forward input and fixed yaw are maintained until the player is within interaction reach.

The report says the lever can be placed directly on either command block. This plan chooses the top of the impulse block so activating it gives the impulse block a rising signal and powers the adjacent repeating block through the powered arrangement.

source_meta._title: The player's vertical motion is reset when moving on the ground

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 1 in a disposable single-player Overworld. Use Creative mode with commands enabled for deterministic command-block setup. Use one player, remain grounded without Creative flight, and perform the test with keyboard-and-mouse movement controls.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can start the exact affected version "26.2 Snapshot 1".
The test world is vanilla, with no mods, data packs, or server plugins that alter player movement or commands.
Only one player is present so every use of @p in the supplied command resolves unambiguously to the test player.
Commands are enabled and the player can place and configure a command block.
Chat messages are visible rather than hidden.
An open, level area of full solid blocks is available, with several unobstructed blocks in front of the player for grounded walking.
The player is not flying, jumping, swimming, climbing, riding an entity, standing in a portal, or affected by anything that independently changes vertical movement.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for the exact affected version "26.2 Snapshot 1", launch it, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 1
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running game as 26.2 Snapshot 1.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a disposable test world in Creative mode. Enable commands if the world-creation screen exposes a separate command or cheats option, then enter the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Allow Commands: On, if shown -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in the Overworld in Creative mode and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally. Locate an open, approximately level area made from full solid blocks. Stand on it while not flying, and face a direction with at least several clear blocks available for later forward movement.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing motionless on a full solid block, is not flying, and has an unobstructed walking path ahead.

steps.action: Ensure in-game chat is visible. If chat is hidden, open the pause menu and change the chat visibility to Shown before returning to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Chat Settings -> Chat: Shown
steps.success_cue: Ordinary chat and tellraw messages can appear in the on-screen chat area.

steps.action: Press T to open chat, enter the command that gives the executing player a command block, and press Enter.
steps.exact_input: /give @s minecraft:command_block
steps.success_cue: A Command Block item is present in the player's inventory or hotbar.

steps.action: Make the Command Block the selected item. If it is not already in the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the screen, press E, move it into a hotbar slot, close the inventory, and select that slot using its number key or the mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E if inventory rearrangement is needed; then select the Command Block's hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Command Block is visibly held in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Without obstructing the clear walking path, aim at the top or side of a nearby solid block and right-click once to place the Command Block. Place it to the side of or behind the intended walking line so the player will not collide with it during the final movement.
steps.exact_input: right-click
steps.success_cue: A Command Block is placed near the player, and the level walking path in front of the player remains unobstructed.

steps.action: Aim at the placed Command Block and right-click it to open its configuration screen.
steps.exact_input: right-click the placed Command Block
steps.success_cue: The command-block configuration screen is open and shows a command input field plus block-mode controls.

steps.action: Set the command block's block type to Repeating, its condition to Unconditional, and its redstone mode to Always Active. A Repeating command block configured as Always Active executes continuously without a redstone clock. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACommand_blocks_and_functions?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Repeating; Unconditional; Always Active
steps.success_cue: The configuration screen displays Repeating, Unconditional, and Always Active.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly in the command input field, including the leading slash and all punctuation, capitalization, brackets, quotation marks, and selector arguments. Click Done to save and activate the repeating command block.
steps.exact_input: /tellraw @p {"nbt":"Motion[1]", "entity":"@p"}
steps.success_cue: The command-block screen closes and a continuing stream of numeric Motion[1] messages begins appearing in chat. Do not evaluate the numeric values yet.

steps.action: If opening or closing the command block changed the view direction, use only the mouse to face the previously selected clear path. Do not press a movement key, Space, or the Creative-flight control. Keep the player near the command block so its chunk remains loaded.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse only if necessary; do not use W, A, S, D, or Space
steps.success_cue: The player remains grounded and stationary beside the active command block, faces an unobstructed path, and numeric chat messages continue.

steps.action: Release all movement and camera input and leave the player completely still for approximately 3 real-time seconds while the repeating command continues running.
steps.exact_input: No keyboard or mouse movement for approximately 3 seconds
steps.success_cue: The player has remained grounded without translating or rotating, and the numeric chat stream has continued throughout the interval.

steps.action: While continuing to avoid W, A, S, D, Space, and other movement controls, move the mouse left and right and then slightly up and down for approximately 2 seconds. This changes only the camera direction; do not click or move the player's position.
steps.exact_input: Move mouse left/right and up/down for approximately 2 seconds; press no movement keys
steps.success_cue: The view direction has changed while the player's feet remain on the same ground position and the numeric chat stream continues.

steps.action: Stop moving the mouse and again provide no keyboard or mouse input for approximately 2 seconds.
steps.exact_input: No keyboard or mouse movement for approximately 2 seconds
steps.success_cue: The player is once again completely stationary and grounded, with the repeating command still producing numeric messages.

steps.action: Press and hold W to begin walking forward along the clear, level ground. Do not press Space, do not start flying, and do not move into water, climbable blocks, or the command block. As soon as grounded forward movement begins, keep W held and hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.exact_input: Press and hold W; do not press Space
steps.success_cue: The player has begun translating forward across level solid ground while remaining grounded, and the repeating tellraw command is still outputting Motion[1].

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just begun grounded forward movement with W held after the required still-camera-still sequence. The Repeating, Unconditional, Always Active command block is continuing to output the player's Motion[1] value; begin observing the command output without changing the movement state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, world seed, coordinates, dimension, world type, or multiplayer requirement. A disposable single-player Creative-mode Overworld is selected as the minimum deterministic setup because it permits command-block placement and configuration.

The report does not state exact durations for either stationary period or the camera movement. Three seconds, two seconds, and two seconds are practical intervals chosen to make each phase distinct while preserving the reported order.
The supplied tellraw command is preserved exactly as written in the report. No attempt was made to modernize its selector, NBT path, or text-component syntax.
The report does not state how the repeating command block should be powered. Always Active is used as the standard deterministic configuration for continuous execution.
Remaining in Creative mode is not asserted to be required by the report. The player must remain grounded and must not enter Creative flight during the movement test.

source_meta._title: Vertical velocity after bouncing does not take drag into consideration

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 1 in a new single-player Creative-mode world with commands enabled. Use an open, level area; a Superflat world is a practical choice but is not required by the report. Creative flight may be used while constructing and resetting the test, but it must be disabled during each bounce trial.
preconditions: Launch exactly 26.2 Snapshot 1, the first version listed as affected; do not use the fix version 26.2 Snapshot 6.
Use a player with permission to run commands. In single-player, create the world with commands/cheats enabled.
Use default player attributes until the report's air_drag_modifier command is executed. Avoid unrelated status effects or equipment that changes movement, gravity, or jumping.
Have at least 16 ordinary full solid blocks for the tower bodies, such as Stone, plus 1 Chest, 4 Slime Blocks, and 2 Enchanting Tables.
Build in an area with several blocks of unobstructed space above the structures and beyond the target towers.
Use the same forward movement input for both comparison trials. Do not use Sprint, Sneak, or Creative flight during either fall and bounce.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 1, launch the game, and wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left or title-screen version text identifies the running game as 26.2 Snapshot 1.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode with commands enabled. A Superflat world may be selected to provide a level construction area. Enter the world and wait until the surrounding terrain is rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Commands/Cheats: On -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded Creative-mode world and can both fly and open the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use its search function to obtain one stack of an ordinary full solid block such as Stone, 4 Slime Blocks, 1 Chest, and 2 Enchanting Tables. Place these items in accessible hotbar slots, then close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: E; search for Stone, Slime Block, Chest, and Enchanting Table
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains all four required block types, including at least 16 full solid blocks.

steps.action: Choose a level area and face one consistent forward direction. Define two adjacent one-block-wide lanes: the left lane will use the six-block source tower, and the right lane will use the source tower with a chest on top. The intended top-down arrangement is a source row, two consecutive rows of slime blocks, and then a target row, with no empty horizontal row between them.
steps.success_cue: There is enough clear space for a structure two blocks wide and four rows long, with at least ten blocks of open air above it.

steps.action: At the source row, build two adjacent vertical columns from the same ground level. Make each column exactly 6 full blocks tall. Keep the columns aligned side by side so that each forms the starting platform for one lane.
steps.exact_input: Place 6 full blocks vertically in the left lane and 6 full blocks vertically in the right lane.
steps.success_cue: Two adjacent six-block-high columns stand at the back of the course, and their top full-block surfaces are level with each other.

steps.action: Place one Chest directly on top of the right source column. Do not place anything on top of the left source column. The left starting surface is therefore the top of the sixth full block, while the right starting surface is the top of the chest above an otherwise identical six-block column.
steps.exact_input: Select Chest; right-click the top face of the right six-block column once.
steps.success_cue: The right source has a chest on top, while the adjacent left source remains exactly six full blocks tall with an exposed top face.

steps.action: At ground level directly in front of the two source columns, place 4 Slime Blocks as a two-by-two square. The rear slime row must be adjacent to the source row, and the pad must extend two blocks forward. Each source lane must line up with one block in each slime row.
steps.exact_input: Place Slime Blocks in both lanes for two consecutive forward rows.
steps.success_cue: A level two-block-wide by two-block-long slime pad is centered directly in front of the two source columns.

steps.action: Directly beyond the front edge of the slime pad, build two adjacent target towers, one aligned with each lane. For each target tower, stack 2 full solid blocks from the same ground level and place an Enchanting Table as the third and top block. Do not add any block above either Enchanting Table.
steps.exact_input: For each lane: place 2 full blocks vertically, then place 1 Enchanting Table on the upper block.
steps.success_cue: Two target towers stand directly beyond the slime pad; each consists of two full blocks with an Enchanting Table as its third block.

steps.action: Inspect the finished course from above while flying. Verify the exact row order: two adjacent source towers; a two-by-two slime pad immediately in front; and two adjacent target towers immediately beyond the slime. Verify that only the right source tower has a chest and that both target towers have Enchanting Tables on top.
steps.success_cue: Both lanes are straight, equally spaced, unobstructed, and identical except that the right source starting surface is the chest above the six-block column.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The command must be run by the same player who will perform the jumps.
steps.exact_input: /attribute @s air_drag_modifier base set 3
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a red syntax or permission error, and command feedback indicates that the executing player's air_drag_modifier base value was set to 3.

steps.action: Ensure Sneak is not active before either trial. Release the Sneak control, normally Left Shift; if Sneak is configured as a toggle, press it as needed to return to the normal standing state. Sneaking must remain inactive when contacting the slime because it suppresses the slime-block bounce. ([ja.minecraft.wiki](https://ja.minecraft.wiki/w/%E3%82%B9%E3%83%8B%E3%83%BC%E3%82%AF?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Release Sneak (default Left Shift).
steps.success_cue: The player is standing at full height and is not in the sneaking/crouching pose.

steps.action: Use Creative flight to reach the exposed top face of the left, six-block source tower. Land near the center of that top face, face straight down the left lane toward its two slime blocks and target Enchanting Table, and disable Creative flight. Keep Sneak and Sprint inactive.
steps.exact_input: Use movement and Creative flight controls to land; double-tap Jump (default Space) if necessary to turn flight off.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary and centered on the exposed top of the left six-block column, facing straight along the left lane, and is no longer flying, sneaking, or sprinting.

steps.action: Perform the lower-source comparison pass. Hold Forward, normally W, and press Jump, normally Space, once to leave the six-block tower. Continue holding Forward without Sprint or Sneak while falling onto the left half of the slime pad and through the resulting rebound. Do not activate Creative flight by double-tapping Jump.
steps.exact_input: Hold W; press Space once; continue holding W.
steps.success_cue: The player contacts a left-lane Slime Block and begins a rebound while continuing forward along the left lane.

steps.action: Allow the lower-source pass to finish without changing the structures or the air_drag_modifier value. Release Forward after the player has passed the target-tower area, then wait until the player is no longer airborne or bouncing.
steps.exact_input: Release W after passing the target area; wait for motion to settle.
steps.success_cue: The first comparison pass is complete and the player is stationary; the course remains unchanged.

steps.action: Use Creative flight to return to the right source tower. Land centered on the top surface of the Chest, face straight down the right lane, and disable flight. Confirm that the command has not been rerun with another value, Sneak is inactive, Sprint is inactive, and the planned input matches the lower-source pass.
steps.exact_input: Fly to the Chest; land; disable flight; release Left Shift and Sprint.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary and centered on top of the chest, facing directly along the right lane, with Creative flight, Sneak, and Sprint all inactive.

steps.action: Perform the taller-source test pass using the same input as the lower-source pass. Hold Forward, normally W, and press Jump, normally Space, once to leave the chest. Continue holding Forward without Sprint or Sneak while falling onto the right half of the slime pad. Hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as slime contact produces the upward rebound.
steps.exact_input: Hold W; press Space once; continue holding W.
steps.success_cue: The player has contacted a right-lane Slime Block after jumping from the chest-topped source and has just begun the upward rebound toward the right target tower.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just begun the upward rebound after contacting the right-lane slime block from the chest-topped source tower. The air_drag_modifier base value remains 3, the player is moving forward without sprinting or sneaking, and the right-lane target Enchanting Table is directly ahead. Begin observing the resulting trajectory from this state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, game mode, tower-body block type, or dedicated-server requirement. A new single-player Creative world and Stone tower bodies are practical execution choices, not report requirements.

The comment says the slime square and target towers are 'in front of' the source towers but does not give numerical horizontal gaps. This plan uses the simplest contiguous interpretation: source row, two slime rows, then target row, with no empty rows between them.

The attached bounce video was named in the report but its visual layout was not included in the supplied content and could not be retrieved through the permitted web sources, so any spacing visible only in that video remains unverified.
The report's 'two 3 block tall towers with the third block being enchantment tables' is interpreted as two full solid blocks with an Enchanting Table placed as the third/top block.

The report does not state which adjacent tower is on the left or right. This plan assigns the plain six-block source to the left lane and the chest-topped source to the right lane solely to keep the procedure deterministic.
The exact horizontal input duration is not specified. This plan holds normal Forward movement through each bounce and prohibits Sprint so both trials use repeatable, matching input.
The lower-source pass is performed first as a comparison trial and the chest-source pass second as the final trigger. The report describes both heights but does not explicitly require this order.

External verification was limited to confirming that Sneak should be inactive because sneaking suppresses slime-block bouncing; no external source was used to replace the report's command, version list, or structure description.

source_meta._title: Sulfur spring geysers can push players in Creative mode who are flying

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.2 Snapshot 5 in a single-player Creative-mode world. Use default controls unless the corresponding actions have been rebound. No specific seed, coordinates, difficulty, graphics setting, server, or additional player is specified by the report.
preconditions: Enable snapshots in the Minecraft Launcher installation settings and create or select an installation for exactly 26.2 Snapshot 5.
Use a world in Creative mode so that the player can obtain the required blocks and activate Creative flight.
Allow the world and nearby chunks to finish loading before constructing the geyser.

The reproduction uses a constructed geyser consisting, from bottom to top, of a Magma Block, a Potent Sulfur block, and one Water source block. The official 26.2 Snapshot 5 description confirms that Potent Sulfur forms a geyser when placed above a Magma Block and below one to four Water source blocks. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-26-2-snapshot-5?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using the launcher installation for exactly 26.2 Snapshot 5. Do not use the listed fix version, 26.2 Snapshot 6.
steps.success_cue: The game reaches the title screen and identifies the running version as 26.2 Snapshot 5.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer and create a new world, or load an existing disposable test world, with the game mode set to Creative. If creating a world, choose Creative on the world-creation screen, create the world, and wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded world in Creative mode and can access the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Move to an open build location with solid ground and unobstructed vertical space. Use a location where the player can clearly see the top of the geyser and hover directly above it.
steps.success_cue: There is a visible ground block on which to build, with open space above the intended geyser column.

steps.action: Press E, or the rebound Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to locate a Magma Block, Potent Sulfur, and a Water Bucket. Move one of each into separate hotbar slots at the bottom of the inventory, then close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: Magma Block; Potent Sulfur; Water Bucket
steps.success_cue: The hotbar contains a Magma Block, Potent Sulfur, and a Water Bucket, and the normal world view is visible.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Magma Block. Aim at the top face of the chosen ground block and use the Place/Use action, right-click by default, once to place the Magma Block.
steps.exact_input: right-click
steps.success_cue: One Magma Block is visible at the base of the intended geyser column.

steps.action: Select Potent Sulfur in the hotbar. Aim at the top face of the placed Magma Block and right-click once, placing the Potent Sulfur directly on top of the Magma Block. This bottom-to-top relationship is required for the periodic geyser configuration in 26.2 Snapshot 5. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-26-2-snapshot-5?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: right-click
steps.success_cue: The Potent Sulfur occupies the block position immediately above the Magma Block, with no intervening block or gap.

steps.action: Select the Water Bucket. Aim at the top face of the Potent Sulfur and right-click once to place water in the block directly above it. The water may flow outward; do not remove the stationary source block located directly over the Potent Sulfur. One Water source block is sufficient for the Snapshot 5 geyser arrangement. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-26-2-snapshot-5?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: right-click
steps.success_cue: A Water source block occupies the position directly above the Potent Sulfur, producing a vertical stack of Magma Block, Potent Sulfur, and Water source from bottom to top.

steps.action: Move clear of the water and quickly press the Jump control twice; the default key is Space. Once Creative flight engages, hold Space briefly to ascend above the water, then release it to hover.
steps.exact_input: Space, Space; then hold Space briefly
steps.success_cue: The player remains suspended when movement keys are released instead of falling, confirming that Creative flight is active.

steps.action: While remaining in Creative flight, use the movement controls to center the player horizontally over the Water source and Potent Sulfur column. Hover close above the water surface—approximately one block above it—so the player is in the unobstructed vertical path of the geyser plume. Release the movement controls after aligning.
steps.exact_input: W/A/S/D as needed; Space to rise; Left Shift to descend
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in Creative flight directly above the center of the geyser column, with the water and Potent Sulfur beneath them.

steps.action: Remain hovering over the same column and wait for a periodic eruption. Do not land, disable flight, or move away. If the geyser erupted before the player was positioned, continue hovering until a later eruption. Proceed the instant the water-particle plume and eruption sound begin beneath the flying player.
steps.success_cue: A geyser eruption has just begun directly beneath the player while the player remains airborne in Creative flight.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is hovering in Creative flight directly above the constructed Magma Block–Potent Sulfur–Water geyser, and a periodic geyser eruption has just begun beneath the player. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, before changing position or flight state.
uncertainties: The report specifies no world seed, coordinates, naturally generated sulfur spring, or required geyser size. The plan therefore uses the simplest officially documented Snapshot 5 construction with one Water source block.
The report does not state that multiplayer or a dedicated server is required, so a single-player Creative world is selected as the minimum deterministic environment.
Magma-powered geyser activation occurs at random intervals in 26.2 Snapshot 5, so the exact waiting time cannot be prescribed; readiness is determined by the eruption particles and sound.
The report does not specify an exact hover height. Approximately one block above the water surface is used as a practical position intended to keep the flying player in the geyser's vertical plume.

source_meta._title: The pick block function doesn't work with entities while in survival or adventure mode

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.7.10 client in a new singleplayer world. Use Creative mode with cheats enabled only to prepare the deterministic test area and inventory, then enter Survival mode before placing and targeting the item frame. No particular seed, coordinates, difficulty, server, resource pack, or graphics setting is required by the report.
preconditions: Use the exact recommended version, Minecraft Java Edition 1.7.10; do not open the test world in a newer version.

The client must have an input assigned to the Pick Block action. The default input is pressing the mouse wheel/middle mouse button, but the configured binding must be used if controls have been changed.
Cheats must be enabled so the historical 1.7.10 /give and /gamemode commands can be executed in chat.

Before triggering Pick Block, one placed item frame must be visible, one additional Item Frame item must remain in the player's hotbar or inventory, and the selected hotbar slot must contain an item other than an item frame.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation for the exact Java Edition version Minecraft 1.7.10, and launch it without gameplay-altering mods.
steps.exact_input: Minecraft 1.7.10
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.7.10 main menu is displayed.

steps.action: Open Options -> Controls and locate the Pick Block action. Confirm that it has an assigned input; its default is the middle mouse button, also described as pressing the mouse wheel. Do not change the binding unless no input is assigned. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Persediaan?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Controls -> Pick Block
steps.success_cue: The executor knows the exact configured input that will issue Pick Block later in the procedure.

steps.action: Return to the main menu and select Singleplayer -> Create New World. Set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and optionally select the Superflat world type to provide a simple level test area. Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: A new singleplayer world is loading with the player initially in Creative mode and commands available.

steps.action: Wait before continuing until the terrain around the player is rendered and movement and camera controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible and the player can move and look around without world-loading interruption.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the exact historical command shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This gives the nearest player exactly two Item Frames; item frames used numeric item ID 389 before the Flattening. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3ACommands/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: /give @p 389 2
steps.success_cue: The player's inventory contains a stack of exactly two Item Frames.

steps.action: Press T again, type the exact command shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This gives two Stone blocks: one will become the item frame's support and the other will be held during the trigger. Stone used numeric ID 1 in this version. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3ACommands/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: /give @p 1 2
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains exactly two Stone blocks in addition to the two Item Frames.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Move the stack of two Item Frames into hotbar slot 1 and the stack of two Stone blocks into hotbar slot 2. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen. Close the inventory with E.
steps.exact_input: E; Item Frames -> hotbar slot 1; Stone -> hotbar slot 2; E
steps.success_cue: Hotbar slot 1 contains two Item Frames, hotbar slot 2 contains two Stone blocks, and no other item occupies either slot.

steps.action: Press 2 to select the Stone in hotbar slot 2. Aim at the top surface of the ground and right-click once to place one Stone block above the ground. Leave at least one vertical side of this block unobstructed and accessible.
steps.exact_input: 2, then right-click once on the ground
steps.success_cue: One Stone block is standing above the surrounding ground with an exposed vertical side, and one Stone item remains in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Press T, enter the exact Minecraft 1.7.10 game-mode command shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter to switch the player to Survival mode. Numeric game-mode value 0 denotes Survival in the historical command syntax. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Talk%3ACommands/Archive_1?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: /gamemode 0
steps.success_cue: The Survival HUD is visible, including health and hunger indicators, and the player is no longer able to use Creative flight.

steps.action: Press 1 to select the two Item Frames in hotbar slot 1. Face the exposed vertical side of the placed Stone block and position the crosshair over the center of that side from normal interaction distance.
steps.success_cue: The Item Frame stack is selected and visible in the player's hand, with a count of two, and the crosshair is on an exposed vertical face of the Stone block.

steps.action: Right-click once on the exposed vertical side of the Stone block to place one item frame while remaining in Survival mode.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once
steps.success_cue: An empty item frame is visibly attached to the Stone block, and one Item Frame item remains in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Press 2 to select the remaining Stone item in hotbar slot 2. Do not move or remove the remaining Item Frame item from hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: The player is visibly holding Stone rather than an Item Frame, while one Item Frame item remains available in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Stand within normal interaction distance of the placed item frame and aim the crosshair directly at the center of the item frame entity. Adjust the view if necessary so the crosshair is on the frame itself rather than on an exposed portion of the Stone support block.
steps.success_cue: The empty placed item frame fills the center of the view, the crosshair is over it, Stone is still selected, and the spare Item Frame remains in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: While keeping the crosshair on the placed item frame, issue the configured Pick Block action exactly once. With default controls, press the mouse wheel/middle mouse button once. Do not scroll the wheel, press a number key, open the inventory, or perform any additional input afterward. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Persediaan?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Pick Block once; default input: middle mouse button
steps.success_cue: One Pick Block input has just been sent while the player is in Survival mode, Stone was selected, a spare Item Frame was present in hotbar slot 1, and the crosshair targeted the placed item frame entity.

stor.handoff_condition: Immediately after step 14, hand control to the observation subsystem before issuing any further input. The player must remain in Survival mode facing the placed item frame, with the Pick Block input just completed and the hotbar state left untouched for evaluation.
uncertainties: The report lists 24w44a in both Affects versions and Fix versions. It was omitted from affected_versions because the report and comments identify 24w44a as the fixing version, and fix versions must not be selected for reproduction.

The formal reproduction steps use Survival mode even though the title and description also mention Adventure mode. This plan follows the simplest deterministic formal path and tests Survival mode only.

The command-based item acquisition, Stone support block, Creative setup phase, and optional Superflat world are practical execution choices; the report requires only two item frames, Survival mode, a placed frame, a non-frame item selected, and Pick Block targeted at the frame.
No seed, coordinates, difficulty, multiplayer server, or exact camera distance was supplied by the report.
A rebound Pick Block control must be used instead of the default middle mouse button if the local control configuration differs.
